findings.failure_mode: missing or unreadable file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| SessionError::Io(e))?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data with non-numeric second field panics the caller instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) with bounded index access via split_once

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O inside data-processing logic
findings.failure_mode: parsing function produces side effects; breaks pure-data contracts, causes non-deterministic output, and violates Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: remove println entirely; logging belongs in the shell layer that calls the pure parser, not inside the parser itself

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use index access without bounds checking; line.split(',').collect() into a Vec allocates unnecessarily and the index is not bounds-safe
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes a panic at index access, and the index is out of bounds when the input has only one field
findings.fix: replace split/collect/index pattern with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) and parse (_name, value_str) = result; avoid index access entirely

findings.problem: (...).parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy as cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: any parsed value above 65535 silently truncates to u16 range, corrupting data without any error or warning
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 with value_str.trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow), or use u16::try_from(u32_val).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) after parse

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/parse), domain construction (Record), and side-effect I/O (println) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: no separation of Data/Calculations/Actions; impossible to test parsing purity; I/O errors and parse errors are conflated; shell concerns leak into data pipeline
findings.fix: split into: (1) pure parse_lines(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> with no I/O or println, (2) shell function load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> that reads the file, calls parser, and handles I/O errors

findings.problem: No bounded allocation: the function collects into Vec with no try_reserve, no domain cap on max rows, and no checked capacity arithmetic
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation from a file path supplied by a caller; a large file consumes arbitrary memory without prior validation
findings.fix: validate a domain cap/max_rows first, create Vec::new(), call values.try_reserve(bounded_cap).map_err(|_| AllocationError::Allocation)? before filling, and reject inputs exceeding the cap

findings.problem: Raw String fields on Record cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly with Record { name: String::from("anything"), value: 0 }
findings.failure_mode: name is unconstrained (no format rules, no length limit); value field has no enforced range; the domain accepts illegal states at construction time
findings.fix: add a parse_boundary function: fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> that validates name format/length and value range via try_from before constructing the domain type
